title.value: List-GRAND: Enhanced Decoding Performance for ORBGRAND with VLSI Implementation
title.justification: The paper discusses the development of List-GRAND (LGRAND), a decoding technique to enhance the performance of ORBGRAND for very large scale integration (VLSI) systems.
title.quote: In this paper, we propose List-GRAND (LGRAND), a technique for boosting the decoding performance of ORBGRAND in order to achieve ML decoding performance comparable to SGRAND.

extractions.description: The paper introduces List-GRAND (LGRAND), a technique designed to improve the decoding performance of Ordered Reliability Bits-GRAND (ORBGRAND). LGRAND aims to achieve maximum likelihood (ML) decoding performance similar to Soft-GRAND (SGRAND), addressing the limitations of parallel hardware implementation. The paper details the VLSI architecture for implementing LGRAND and compares its performance to existing GRAND variants, showing improvements in decoding accuracy and hardware efficiency.

secondary_categories.quote: SGRAND delivers Maximum Likelihood (ML) decoding performance but is not suitable for parallel hardware implementation. ORBGRAND is suitable for parallel hardware implementation, however its decoding performance is inferior to SGRAND.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not address any specific sub-categories related to climate change or environmental issues, as its focus is technical improvement in VLSI systems.
primary_sub_category.quote: The VLSI implementation results show that the proposed LGRAND can achieve an average information throughput of 47.27 − 51.36 Gbps for linear block codes of length 127/128 and different code-rates.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: In line with the primary sub-category, the paper does not touch upon sub-categories concerning environmentally related technologies or applications.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Numerical simulation results show that the proposed LGRAND achieves a 0.5 − 0.75dB performance gain over ORBGRAND for channel codes of different classes (BCH, CA-Polar, and CRC) at a target FER of 10^{-7}.
